A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of cytoplasmic TDP-43 immunoreactivity in the hypoglassal nucleus is a highly sensitive (98%) and specific (100%) biomarker for the pathological diagnosis of amyotrophic laterial sclerosis.

the presence of cytoplasmic TDP-43 immunoreactivity in the hypoglassal nucleus is sufficient to diagnose clinical amyotrophic sclerosis and the severity of cytoplasm TDP-43 deposition in the anterior cingular cortex is sufficient to diagnose behavioral variant frontotempora dementia.

the presence of cytoplasmic TDP-43-positive pathological inclusions in the hypoglassal nucleus is highly specific for clinical amyotrophic laterial sclerosis and that the severity of TPD-43 in the cingulate cortex is highly specific for behavioural variant frontotemporaldementia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pathological identification of the clinical phenotypes of amyotrophic laterial sclerosis and behavioural variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration may be achieved by the assessment of the presence and severity of cytoplasmic TDP-43 deposits in two key regions of the brain, the hypoglossus nucleus and the anterior cingulated cortex, respectively.
a more standardized approach for assessing the regional distribution and severity of TPD-43 pathology can improve the pathological diagnosis of clinical phenotypes.
the presence of pathological TDP-43 is a necessary condition to make the diagnosis of amyotrophic lateralsclerosis and behavioural variant fronto-temporal dementia.
